bullets: Weak: ‘Macbeth is ambitious and this leads to his downfall.’ (obvious, plot-based)
Good: ‘Shakespeare presents ambition as the force that destroys Macbeth.’ (an idea, but no ‘why’)

Grade 9: ‘Shakespeare presents ambition not as a sin imposed by the Witches but as a choice Macbeth makes knowingly, so that his tragedy warns a Jacobean audience that rebellion against a God-appointed king is self-destroying.’

callouts.p: Shakespeare presents [topic] as [concept/idea], [twist: not X but Y / at first… but later…], in order to [purpose for the Jacobean audience].

core.p: A thesis is a one or two sentence argument that answers the question for the whole play. It should be **conceptual** (about an idea, not a plot event), **arguable** (someone could disagree), and include **Shakespeare’s purpose** (why he wrote it this way for a Jacobean audience).

head: Topic
Thesis
rows: Macbeth

Shakespeare presents Macbeth as a brave, self-aware man who chooses evil despite understanding it fully, so that his fall becomes both a warning against regicide and a tragedy about how a conscience can be destroyed.
Lady Macbeth

Shakespeare presents Lady Macbeth as a woman who tries to reject her nature to gain power, yet her collapse shows that the natural order of gender and conscience cannot be overturned without self-destruction.
Banquo

Banquo is Macbeth’s foil: hearing the same prophecy, he resists temptation, showing the Jacobean audience, and King James, Banquo’s descendant, that virtue lies in choosing not to act on dark suggestions.
Macduff
Macduff embodies loyalty to Scotland and a fuller masculinity that includes grief, so his victory represents the restoration of both rightful order and humane values.
The Witches
The Witches tempt rather than control: Shakespeare uses them to explore a Jacobean fear of the supernatural while placing responsibility firmly on Macbeth’s choices.
Duncan and Malcolm

Duncan represents the trusting, holy king of divine right and Malcolm the wiser king who has learned from his father’s mistakes; together they frame Macbeth’s tyranny as an unnatural interruption of order.

head: Topic
Thesis
rows: Ambition
Shakespeare presents ‘vaulting ambition’ as a force that promises greatness but produces only fear and emptiness, warning that ambition which defies divine order ends in ‘nothing’.
Guilt
Shakespeare shows guilt as inescapable: the characters who deny it most fiercely are the ones it destroys, as blood, sleep and darkness imagery turn their crimes into psychological torment.
Fate and free will
Shakespeare deliberately leaves the Witches’ power ambiguous, but every decisive act is Macbeth’s own, so the play argues that fate may tempt, but humans choose.
Kingship
Shakespeare contrasts the holy, healing kingship of Duncan, Edward and Malcolm with Macbeth’s paranoid tyranny to celebrate divine-right monarchy for King James.
Masculinity
Shakespeare questions Lady Macbeth’s equation of manhood with violence, offering through Macduff a definition of manhood that includes feeling.
Appearance and reality
From ‘Fair is foul’ to ‘False face must hide’, Shakespeare shows a world where deception is the means of evil, reflecting Jacobean anxieties about equivocation after the Gunpowder Plot.
Violence and disorder
Shakespeare presents violence as spreading outward from one murder into nature and society, showing the Great Chain of Being collapsing until rightful order is restored.
The supernatural
The supernatural in Macbeth both terrifies and tests: daggers, ghosts and apparitions externalise guilt and temptation, leaving the audience unsure whether evil is outside or inside the human mind.

bullets: Example: ‘not imposed by the Witches but chosen’ → P1: Act 1 Scene 3, the idea of murder is his. P2: Act 1 Scene 7, he decides against and then chooses. P3: Acts 3–4, he seeks out the Witches and acts on ‘firstlings’ of his heart. P4: Act 5, self-awareness in ‘Tomorrow’ and the purpose (warning to the audience).
core.p: Each thesis has two or three ‘moves’. Turn each move into a paragraph.

model: Contrast Macbeth’s betrayal with Banquo, Macduff and Malcolm
Concept: loyalty to the rightful king and to Scotland vs loyalty to self
Purpose: Jacobean audience after the Gunpowder Plot; divine right
exam.q: Write a grade 9 thesis for: ‘How does Shakespeare present the theme of loyalty in Macbeth?’
exam.tip: Name at least two characters in the thesis to show range.

mistakes.r: State an idea and Shakespeare’s purpose.
mistakes.w: Retelling the plot as a thesis.

mistakes.r: Make sure each paragraph proves part of it.
mistakes.w: A thesis that only one paragraph supports.

summary: A bank of grade 9 thesis statements for every likely Macbeth topic: each is a conceptual, arguable sentence that answers ‘how’ and ‘why’, which you can adapt in the first two minutes of the exam.
